title: EOS — focused completion outcome gate correction
intent:
Implement the smallest focused correction for the completion-status defect from #834/#835 after #836 exceeded the 40-turn runtime ceiling. Do not rediscover the repository broadly.

Required work:
Add a deterministic outcome-completion gate so worker/process completion is not sufficient for EOS COMPLETE.

Required behavior:
- #834-like outcome: required Bash/test/worker capability denied before requested cycles execute => BLOCKED, never COMPLETE.
- #835-like outcome: implementation exists but required governed patch/PR/artifact was not produced => BLOCKED or AWAITING_ARTIFACTIZATION-equivalent, never COMPLETE.
- Genuine satisfied execution with required result/evidence => COMPLETE.
- COMPLETE must require the request's expected completion evidence/artifact class, not merely worker.phase === COMPLETE or exit code 0.
- Structured execution/tool/artifact evidence is authoritative; worker text may corroborate but free-text keyword matching alone is insufficient.
- Preserve current Gateway/Verifier correction limits, Claude routing, Cortex READ_ONLY_PILOT, integration authority, and cost/capacity semantics.

Implementation guidance to reduce runtime turns:
1. Start by reading the listed files directly. Do not run repo-wide find/grep discovery unless one exact import/call-site is unresolved.
2. Add the smallest status/outcome contract extension needed; avoid architecture redesign.
3. Add focused regression fixtures for #834, #835, and positive COMPLETE.
4. Run only the directly affected node test files first; run broader EOS contract tests only after focused tests pass.
5. If the required caller is outside the listed files, identify the exact path from imports/usages and add only that path to scope.

Completion:
Produce a governed patch/result or draft PR with the focused correction and tests. Report changed files, focused and broader tests, exact mapping of #834/#835 to corrected status, and whether it is safe to merge. Do not merge automatically. Do not rerun #834/#835 in this issue.
scope: Primary files to inspect first and keep scope narrow unless direct call-site evidence requires one adjacent file:
the exact runtime/artifactization caller that passes worker outcome into deriveStatusState/buildIntakeStatus, if needed.
Do not search unrelated workflows, providers, Agent Manager, Taylor product code, or project-keystone.
